method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across the Báb’s warnings about Him Whom God shall make manifest, Bahá’u’lláh’s testimony of exile, calumny and violence, the test of recognition and the appeal to fair proof, the repeated pattern of earlier communities, the veils of names, leadership and inherited interpretation, and the disciplines of fairness, forbearance, steadfastness and wise teaching. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: Today Satan calls out in the name of the All-Merciful, and the deniers among the people of the Bayan are busily engaged in leading people astray with the utmost deceit and guile.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s warning that Satan calls out in the name of the All-Merciful as the deniers lead people astray with deceit.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! On that Day which is the King of Days, God forbid that you should cling to your divines and leaders and thus remain deprived of the Goal
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s warning not to cling to divines and leaders on the King of Days; addresses authority as a veil.

selected.text: Consider the people of the Bayan and their lack of understanding. They have denied Him by Whose name the heaven of the Bayan was adorned with the sun of wisdom and exposition.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s note that the people of the Bayan denied Him by Whose name the heaven of the Bayan was adorned with the sun of wisdom.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Glory lieth not in placing green and white turbans upon your heads. Were glory to lie in this, then the camel that carrieth them from town to town should glory over all the worlds, for it beareth a thousand times what ye wind round your heads, O heedless ones!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image that glory lies not in green and white turbans, or the camel that carries them would glory over all the worlds; a memorable rebuke to outward status.

selected.text: Thus doth He speak between heaven and earth and address the idolaters among the people of the Bayan, yet they are in mighty veils. … O people of the Bayan! This is the Trust of the All-Merciful with which We have given you glad tidings at all times. Yet when He came to you with the truth, you denied Him
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s address that this is the Trust of the All-Merciful of which they were given glad tidings, yet they denied Him when He came.

selected.text: Among the people are those who recite the Qur'an yet deny Him Who revealed it in truth - they are indeed among the abased. And among them are those who recite the Bayan yet deny the All-Merciful … And among them are those who said He came before the appointed time, thereby objecting to Him through Whom the decree of the appointed time was established between the heavens and the earth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s portrait of those who recite the Qur’an or the Bayan yet deny the One Who revealed it, and of those who object that He came before the appointed time.

selected.text: Know thou that most of the people of the Bayan have turned away from God and disbelieved in Him in Whom they had believed, and have clung to the cord of idle fancies and followed the ways of the deluded ones. We have found no people on earth more heedless than these, even after We commanded them in all the Tablets not to cling to anything created between the heavens and the earth at the time of the Manifestation. They have veiled themselves from those days with all things and have taken idle fancy as their lord instead of God, and thus were they among the prodigal.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that most of the people of the Bayan clung to idle fancies after being commanded in all the Tablets to cling to nothing created at the time of the Manifestation.

selected.text: Though it is observed with absolute certainty that the existing ears are incapable of hearing, and likewise the eyes are not worthy of beholding. The people have become familiar with vain imaginings and idols. Consider the people of Persia: for one thousand two hundred years they spoke of vain imaginings, clung to vain imaginings, and held fast to their hem. And after the manifestation of their ignorance and heedlessness on the Day of Judgment, again the people of Bayan cling to and utter the same vain imaginings.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s reflection that the people of Persia clung to vain imaginings for twelve hundred years and the people of the Bayan cling to the same; frames inherited habit.

selected.text: God's wrath pursueth them, yet they rejoice. Are they the people of faith? Nay, by my Lord, the Most Merciful! The Bayan curseth them, yet they are thunderstruck.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of a people who rejoice while God’s wrath pursues them, and whom the Bayan curses.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! If ye follow your vain imaginings, what is the difference between you and the people of the Furqan? Be fair in truth and be not of the wrongdoers.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s question what difference remains between the people of the Bayan and the people of the Furqan if they follow vain imaginings.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful, and be not of the transgressors. The verses have filled the East and the West of the earth. Judge fairly concerning that which hath appeared in truth, and be not of the wrongdoers
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to judge fairly, since the verses have filled the East and the West; a concise appeal to fairness.

selected.text: Fear ye God, O people of the Bayan, and harm him not through your selfish desires and passions, neither slay him with the swords of your tongues, nor be ye tyrannical and wicked
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to the people of the Bayan not to harm a certain soul through selfish desires or slay him with the swords of the tongue.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Fear the Most Merciful and follow not those who have denied God's signs and His proof, and who turned away from Him when He came with manifest sovereignty.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel not to follow those who denied God’s signs and turned away when He came with manifest sovereignty; a short practical warning.

selected.text: But alas, a hundred times alas, that the people of the Criterion and the people of the Bayan fell into the valley of ignorance and deprivation and, like bats, denied that shining moon.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s lament that the people of the Criterion and of the Bayan, like bats, denied the shining moon; a memorable image.

selected.text: Now again the people of the Bayan are clinging to those same vain imaginings … God protect us and you from the evil of the barking ones who prevent people from this straight and manifest Path
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s note that the people of the Bayan cling to the same vain imaginings, with a prayer for protection from those who keep people from the path.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! On the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, take ye heed lest ye behave like unto them, for ye have believed in Him and in His words and are among those who are certain.
selected.reason: The Báb’s counsel that on the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest the people of the Bayan take heed lest they behave like earlier peoples.

selected.text: Today the people of Bayan are seen to be the most veiled of all people, for they cling to vain imaginings and hold fast to idle fancies. To this beareth witness the Book of God, the Mighty, the All-Knowing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the people of the Bayan are today the most veiled of all, clinging to vain imaginings.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Where were ye when the Light was shining forth from the Supreme Horizon and the Manifestation was standing before the faces of all peoples? Fear God, O ye manifestations of idle fancies!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s question where the people of the Bayan were when the Light shone forth and the Manifestation stood before all peoples.

selected.text: Now again the people of the Bayan are walking those same steps. Say: O heedless ones! Reflect upon the fruits of the previous party, that perchance ye may become aware and roll up the carpet of suspicions and imaginings in the name of the Lord of all names.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to reflect on the fruits of the previous party and roll up the carpet of suspicions in the name of the Lord of all names.

selected.text: O people of God! The enemies lie in wait and strive to extinguish the divine light. Those who have turned away from the Bayan are observed to be far baser than those who turned away from the Qur'an. They have manifested an oppression without peer or likeness
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s warning that those who turned from the Bayan appear baser than those who turned from the Qur’an and have shown an oppression without peer.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! We have sent down for you the verses and manifested the clear proofs, and ye were commanded to that which would draw you nigh unto the supreme horizon. Ye cast behind you that which ye were commanded and took up that which caused the Faithful Spirit to lament.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the people of the Bayan cast behind them what they were commanded and took up what caused the Faithful Spirit to lament.

selected.text: Now the people of the Bayan are occupied with those same vain imaginings. They have not reflected even this much on what was the outcome of the deeds of the Shi'ihs and what was their fruit. By God's life! They are accounted as transgressors in the Book of God, the True, the Manifest King.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s observation that the people of the Bayan have not reflected on the outcome of the deeds of the Shi’ihs.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Are you content to cling to vain imaginings like the people of former times throughout the ages, and ultimately to occupy yourselves with cursing and denouncing from pulpits the One Who is your Goal and Beloved, and to issue decrees for the shedding of His most pure blood?
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s question whether the people of the Bayan are content to curse their Beloved from pulpits and decree His blood, as former peoples did.

selected.text: O most remote of all creatures! By what testimony did ye believe in the Bayan, and by what testimony did ye turn away from Him from Whose horizon shone forth the Sun of divine exposition? What aileth you? How do ye judge? Soon shall ye witness that which ye now deny. Fear God and be not among the lowly ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s question by what testimony they believed in the Bayan and by what testimony they turned from the Sun of divine exposition.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful, and follow not every rejected transgressor and every veiled heedless one … Where, at last, hath fairness gone, and what hath become of justice? Through a brackish drop they deprived themselves of the Euphrates of mercy and were forbidden from the ocean of bounty
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s question where fairness and justice have gone, as people deprive themselves of the Euphrates of mercy through a brackish drop.

selected.text: Those who object to the Self of thy Lord, and yet make mention of the Point of the Bayan - these dwell in the depths of the fire, and these, on that day, cast behind the veil of passion, are thrown upon the dust of self. … Say: O people! Do ye make mention of the Sovereign of the Bayan while disbelieving in His Self
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s rebuke to those who mention the Point of the Bayan while objecting to and disbelieving in His Self; names the contradiction of devotion without recognition.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Fear God and be conscious of Him in your own selves, such that ye neither associate with him, nor feel comfort in his presence, nor sit with him in gathering, nor be of the heedless ones. Flee from him unto God, your Lord, that God may protect you from him and from his evil and from his hosts.
selected.reason: Lawh-i-Hadi counselling the people of the Bayan to flee from a certain misleading figure and not sit with him; a practical safeguard.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Be the glory of the Point of the Bayan by entering into the religion of Him Whom God shall make manifest. Be content with your own effacement, else at the time of the appearance of Him Who shall appear after Him Whom God shall make manifest, to that same degree your existence will bear no fruit.
selected.reason: The Báb’s call to be the glory of the Point of the Bayan by entering the religion of Him Whom God shall make manifest and to be content with self-effacement.

selected.text: By God's life, the Bayan lamenteth for what ye have perpetrated. Though divine counsel leaveth no impression and heavenly admonition beareth no fruit, for God's wrath hath seized them and the recompense of their deeds hath deprived
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s lament that the Bayan mourns what its people have done, though divine counsel leaves no impression on them.

selected.text: Transgress not the bounds of the Bayan, for God hath angels to the measure that ye exceed who will take vengeance on you. And be watchful on the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest lest ye judge those who believe in Him by the bounds of the Bayan, for on that Day all sovereignty belongeth in truth unto Him, and all abide by His command.
selected.reason: Words of the Báb in the Book of Names forbidding believers to judge those who believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest by the bounds of the Bayan; sets the guide’s first safeguard.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Fear the All-Merciful and shed not the blood of Him Who aided you through the nights and days with the hosts of revelation and inspiration. When the Remembrance reached this point, I heard the lamentation of My Most Exalted Pen, whereby arose the wailing of the Most Exalted Paradise and the Crimson Ark, and the eyes of the righteous shed tears.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s plea not to shed the blood of Him Who aided them, with the lament of the Most Exalted Pen and the tears of the righteous; carries the guide’s note of grief.

selected.text: Vain imaginings have deprived the world of the lights of the Luminary of certitude. The vain imaginings of the Shi'ih sect have been renewed, for the deniers of the Bayan cling to the conjectures of that sect. Glory be to God! What strange intoxication has seized the people of the Bayan! They have witnessed and heard the verses of God at all times, yet remain heedless and turn away.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s lament over the strange intoxication of the people of the Bayan, who renew the conjectures of the Shi’ih sect while hearing the verses of God.

selected.text: The deniers of the Bayan have recently desired to move and speak contrary to the Will of God. They have chosen for themselves the station of the Shi'ih. Alas for the servants! Their deeds give them the lie but they perceive it not; their words deny them but they know it not. They were previously Shi'ih - what then was the cause of their avoidance of it, and what now is the reason for choosing it again?
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s observation that the deniers have chosen the station of the Shi’ih again, and His question why they left it and now choose it.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! When ye attain unto the presence of that Day, hasten ye unto Him and question not concerning Him any lying sinner or one possessed of knowledge. Say: Beware lest ye deal with Him as ye dealt with the Point when He appeared with a manifest Book. Fear ye God and spread not corruption in His Cause, nor visit upon Him what ye visited upon this servant, for this was indeed a grievous error in the Mother Book.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel, voiced as the Point, to hasten to Him on that Day and not ask any lying sinner or learned one about Him; a practical rule of independent recognition.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Slay Me not with the swords of your rejection. I have come to you with the remembrance of God, your Lord and the Lord of all worlds. Fear God, O people, and spread not corruption in the earth after its reformation, and shed not blood. Thus has God commanded you in tablets of manifest glory. … Dispute not concerning the verses of God after their revelation, and consume not the property of others unjustly
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s plea not to slay Him with the swords of rejection, shed blood or consume property unjustly; joins recognition with ethical conduct.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Be fair, by God, your Lord, the All-Merciful! Setting aside this divine Servant and the manifestations of eternal glory revealed in this Revelation, consider ye the entire Bayan and judge for yourselves. You who were not content with the judgment of Truth and what was sent down from His presence - yet Truth, if justice be observed, is content with your judgment, that perchance an eye might open in fairness and turn toward God.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s appeal to the people of the Bayan to be fair and judge the matter by the entire Bayan; models the test of fairness the guide returns to.

selected.text: Verily He hath ever been the Preserver of all things. Say: Verily God shall distinguish between all His servants at every Resurrection. Will ye not fear God? Enter ye, then, into that which God hath ordained for you in every Dispensation, and be not veiled from God by that which ye acquired in your former manifestations. Pronounce that Name upon those who believe not in God, your Lord, and who follow not what hath been sent down in the Bayan, if ye desire to behold them abased beneath your feet. Say: God shall, verily, seize with a severe seizing those who have not believed in God and His signs
selected.reason: The Báb’s counsel not to be veiled from God by what was acquired in former manifestations, since God distinguishes His servants at every Resurrection; states the principle of renewal.

selected.text: all examine within themselves how they seek aid from God, their Lord. Yet they comprehend not the workings of God's command, nor do they seek His aid. Say: The aid of God in the day of Muhammad was that which was revealed in the Qur'an. They who embraced Islam were aided thereby. But they who remained bound to their scriptures received naught of their Lord's aid, though they perceive it not. Fear ye God, O people of the Bayan, lest ye be veiled from Him Whom God shall make manifest on the Day of Resurrection, whereby the aid of the All-Merciful would be cut off from you while ye know it not. Say: His aid lieth in His words, through which ye are created and
selected.reason: The Báb’s explanation that divine aid in Muhammad’s day lay in the Qur’an, and His warning that the people of the Bayan may be cut off from that aid if veiled from the next Manifestation.

selected.text: O leaders of the Bayan! Fear ye God, and let not leadership prevent you from this bounty on this Day. Be not proud before God in what ye possess, but hasten ye to the shore of a wondrous Name. Trust not in that Day in your deeds or your actions, but trust in the grace that shineth from the horizon of holy radiance. Even now I witness that some among you take up prayer beads in your hands and make mention of God therewith, yet every morning and evening ye pronounce judgment against God Who created you.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to the leaders of the Bayan not to let leadership prevent them, with the image of those who hold prayer beads yet judge against God; addresses authority and piety.

selected.text: For in the presence of Him Whom God shall make manifest thou art equal - if thou believest in Him thou shalt enter beneath the shadow of Affirmation, and if thou art veiled from Him thou shalt enter beneath the shadow of Negation, even after having professed the unity of God thy Lord throughout thy life and having watched over thyself in thy religion lest thou transgress its bounds before God manifests the Manifestation of His Self. For at the time of thy transgression thou art in a fire worse than being veiled. And if thou lookest into all religions, thou seest the dwellers of His paradise and His fire through their following the bounds of their religion or
selected.reason: The Báb’s teaching that before Him Whom God shall make manifest belief places one under Affirmation and veiling under Negation, whatever one’s lifelong devotion; makes the choice personal.

selected.text: By the life of God! The opposers among the people of the Bayan appear more veiled than all other peoples. They have returned to the first step. They speak according to their desires and by them seek to prove their case against God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s observation that the opposers speak according to their desires and use them as proof against God; names the epistemic problem at the heart of rejection.

selected.text: Glory be to God! Despite this, the followers of the Bayan are seen to be the most ignorant of all peoples and the most heedless of all religions. They have failed to comprehend the Day of God and remain heedless and veiled from that which the All-Merciful revealed in the Bayan. Souls who have not attained even a drop from the ocean of knowledge, like the opposer from Kirman and his followers, have wandered through valleys of fancy and idle imagination, remaining deprived and forbidden from the lights of the Morn of certitude.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s description of followers of the Bayan, like the opposer from Kirman, wandering in valleys of fancy and remaining heedless of the Day of God.

selected.text: I swear by the Sun of the horizon of sanctification that the people of the Bayan appear more veiled than the people of the Furqan. After all exertions and the rending of veils, it is observed that this people cling to, hold fast to, and utter the same words which that rebellious and insolent group before them spoke.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s oath that, after all the rending of veils, the people of the Bayan repeat the words of the group before them.

selected.text: Today it behoveth each one of the people of God to pass beyond the gulf of names, through divine strength and power, that they may find their way to the Most Great Ocean. Consider ye the peoples of former ages and centuries: certain souls who clung to names and who, night and day, occupied themselves with disputation and opposition, accounting themselves the most learned of all peoples and the most excellent of all nations. Yet when the dawn of the Day of His Manifestation broke forth and the Intended One appeared, all arose to shed His pure blood, save a few among the Shaykhis who attained
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to pass beyond the gulf of names, recalling learned souls of former ages who rose to shed the Intended One’s blood; a foundational call.

selected.text: you believed in Him-them who had crushed the idols of vain imaginings with My exalted power, and abandoned the bastion of blind imitation and perversity in My Name, the All-Powerful, the All-Subduing, the Almighty. No sooner have ye believed in Me and acknowledged My sovereignty and recognized My book, than We admonished you in all Our Tablets not to act as the infidels amongst our heedless servants had done. And We revealed not the Bayan but to announce unto you Our appearance in the kingdom of all creation. And when the Lord of Divine Decree manifested Himself once again and appeared on the clouds of Divine behest, you denied Him and rejected that which you had believed in, and turned away from
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s reminder that He revealed the Bayan only to announce His appearance, and that when He appeared again they rejected what they had believed.

selected.text: Then know that most of the people of the Bayan are still being nourished from the breast of heedlessness and ignorance - their weaning time has not yet come, much less their maturity. Thus have We been witness. Behold their lack of understanding and knowledge! They claim belief in the previous Manifestation, yet from My Own Self they remain veiled. They read My words, yet remain heedless of their Revealer. They cite My previous verses as proof against Me, though all of them proceeded from the Point of the Mouth of My all-pervading, all-encompassing Will.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the people of the Bayan still nursing at the breast of heedlessness, citing His earlier verses as proof against Him; a distinctive image of immaturity.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Fear the All-Merciful and follow not your idle fancies. Follow the Truth, the Knower of things unseen, Who hath come from the horizon of power with the standards of His signs. Read, then be fair, and be not of those who behold the light yet deny it. That which was never manifest in the world hath appeared, and He hath come through Whose remembrance the Bayan was adorned, and before it the Qur'an, and before it the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms. Beware lest ye deprive yourselves of that which hath been manifested in truth. Cast away the people and what they possess, then your conjectures and imaginings.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to read, be fair, and cast away conjectures, since He has come by Whose remembrance the Bayan, the Qur’an and earlier Books were adorned.

selected.text: For twelve hundred years the people of the Furqan clung to vain imaginings and idle fancies, depriving the servants of God from all the infinite divine bounties and heavenly sustenance, such that, as was witnessed, those imaginings and fancies caused the martyrdom of the Primal Point, may the spirit of all else but Him be sacrificed for His sake. I swear by the Sun of certitude that those fancies have been and will continue to be the cause and reason for the kindling of the fire of tyranny throughout the world
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s teaching that twelve hundred years of vain imaginings caused the martyrdom of the Primal Point and kindle tyranny in the world.

selected.text: O divines of the Bayan! Reject not one another in your questions, for God your Lord hath strictly forbidden this. Speak with modesty and write with modesty. If ye witness against anyone at a lower degree while placing yourselves at a higher degree, attract him with gracious words. For throughout your nights ye are magnified in God's shelter and protection, but on the first Day of Resurrection ye shall be tested. Should ye err in your questions and God wish to pardon you, naught shall diminish from your merit. Believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest, that He may correct all wherein ye err. But if ye err not even by a single letter in your words, yet should God wish to cast you into the fire and nullify your deeds, none could prevent it.
selected.reason: The Báb’s charge to the divines of the Bayan to question with modesty, attract others with gracious words and believe in Him Who will correct their errors; an ethical antidote to rejection.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Now doth the Tongue of God speak from the Most Exalted Horizon, saying: O people of the earth! By what proof did ye believe in 'Ali aforetime, when He came with sovereign authority and was surrounded by the hosts of manifest glory? If ye believed in Him through the verses sent down unto Him from the immortal Kingdom - divine and wondrous verses - then by God, this is My Self and these are My verses that have filled the horizons with their splendor! Why then do ye disbelieve in that which ye believed in before, hovering on the brink of repudiation, though We counseled you in all the Tablets, nay in every line, to let nothing that hath been created between earth and heaven veil you at the time of His Manifestation?
selected.reason: Suriy-i-Fath asking by what proof the people believed in ‘Ali aforetime, and why they disbelieve in the same kind of verses now; a foundational argument from consistency.

selected.text: For most of the people of the Bayan are fit only to worship the calf rather than prostrate before the Truth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s stark image that most of the people of the Bayan are fit only to worship the calf rather than prostrate before the Truth.

selected.text: At times they cling to the Qur'an and at times to the Bayan, desiring to spread the carpet of past imaginings
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s note that opponents cling at times to the Qur’an and at times to the Bayan to spread the carpet of past imaginings.

selected.text: And the people of the Bayan pray and fast, but every hour they shot thousands of arrows at the illumined breast.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s observation that the people of the Bayan pray and fast while shooting thousands of arrows at the illumined breast; a stark contrast of piety and persecution.

selected.text: Yet there befell Him at the hands of the wicked ones who claim adherence to the Bayan that which the worlds cannot bear.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s brief testimony that what befell Him at the hands of those claiming adherence to the Bayan the worlds cannot bear.

selected.text: The people of the Bayan have cast aside their Lord and taken hold of that which was commanded unto them by every crafty deceiver
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s note that the people of the Bayan cast aside their Lord for what every crafty deceiver commanded.

selected.text: O Lord! Thou seest how the people of the Bayan have broken Thy Covenant and violated Thy Testament and turned away from Thy Beauty.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that the people of the Bayan have broken God’s Covenant and turned from His Beauty.

selected.text: Blessed is he who accepts, whom neither the doubts of the people of the Bayan deterred, nor the clamor of the oppressors frightened
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s blessing on one whom neither the doubts of the people of the Bayan nor the clamor of oppressors deterred.

selected.text: Were I to mention when the people of the Bayan rose up against Me - by God, I witnessed from them what no eye in creation hath witnessed.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s testimony that He witnessed from the people of the Bayan what no eye in creation has witnessed.

selected.text: The harm to the Beloved of all creation came from the people of the Bayan who, with the utmost effort and struggle, arose to waste away the Cause
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the harm to the Beloved came from the people of the Bayan who strove to waste away the Cause.

selected.text: The people of the Bayan waxed proud against Him - some denied and turned away, some arose in hypocrisy, and some pronounced their verdict against Him.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s summary that some denied, some arose in hypocrisy and some pronounced verdict against Him.

selected.text: O leaders of the Bayan, do ye deny Him through Whom your realities were created and your names were exalted? Fear God and be steadfast in the Cause.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s question to the leaders of the Bayan whether they deny Him through Whom their realities were created and their names exalted.

selected.text: Yet the people of the Bayan rejected Me after I came unto them from the Orient of divine knowledge with verses that all the books of the world cannot match
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the people of the Bayan rejected Him though He came with verses all the books of the world cannot match.

selected.text: Doth it beseem anyone to cling to the Bayan in his turning away from God, or to use it as proof when the All-Merciful hath come with His mighty kingdom
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s question whether it beseems anyone to cling to the Bayan or use it as proof in turning away from God.

selected.text: Verily, We behold the people of the Bayan who have turned away from the All-Merciful to be in greater loss than they on God's Day, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.

selected.text: Beware, beware lest the doubts of the people of the Bayan prevent thee from drawing nigh unto God, the Lord of existence. Beware, beware lest that which hath been revealed in the Bayan veil thee.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s twofold warning not to let the doubts of the people of the Bayan, or what was revealed in the Bayan itself, veil one from God.

selected.text: Beware lest ye be saddened by what hath befallen the chosen ones of God at the hands of those who claim adherence to the Bayan. Verily, the All-Merciful is quit of them, and the Bayan doth curse them.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s comfort not to be saddened by what befell God’s chosen ones, for the All-Merciful is quit of their oppressors and the Bayan curses them.

selected.text: For We have found the people of the Bayan to be like the people of the Furqan, nay rather more veiled, if ye but knew. They speak as others spoke before and act as did the nations of old. Soon shall ye know.
selected.reason: Lawh-i-Ibna’ likening the people of the Bayan to the people of the Furqan, speaking as others spoke before; a concise statement of the repeated pattern.

selected.text: He counseled the servants and those in the Bayan to this Revelation that hath appeared from the horizon of the world, but the people of the Bayan violated God's Covenant and turned away from the Lord of nations.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s note that the Báb counselled those in the Bayan toward this Revelation, yet they violated God’s Covenant.

selected.text: Take ye My choice sealed wine in My Name, the Self-Subsisting, then drink thereof in despite of the people of the Bayan who have turned away from the All-Merciful and disbelieved in God, the Lord of all worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s invitation to drink His choice sealed wine in His Name in despite of the people of the Bayan who turned away.

selected.text: When We revealed a mystery from Our Most Great Mystery with clear proof and evidence, the people of the Bayan fell stunned upon the dust of idle fancy. Thus was the matter decreed by One Who is All-Knowing, All-Informed.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that when a mystery was revealed with clear proof the people of the Bayan fell stunned upon the dust of idle fancy.

selected.text: Observe thou the people of the Bayan and their veils, and that to which they have clung after We commanded them to cling to naught of all that hath been created between the heavens and the earth at the time of the Manifestation.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to observe the veils of the people of the Bayan after they were commanded to cling to nothing at the time of the Manifestation.

selected.text: This is the Beloved of the All-Merciful, Who hath been afflicted at the hands of the people of the Bayan - they who claim to believe in that which was revealed aforetime yet have denied Him around Whom circle the Kingdom of Verses
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s description of the Beloved afflicted by those who claim to believe in what was revealed aforetime.

selected.text: Among the deniers are they who cling to the Bayan and turn away from the All-Merciful. These are assuredly the companions of the fire. Say: By God! Whoso denieth this Cause shall never be able to establish any cause in all creation.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s declaration that whoever denies this Cause can never establish any cause in all creation; a foundational argument.

selected.text: But when the Cause became somewhat manifest, the deniers among the people of the Bayan again became occupied with the same vain imaginings. Blessed are those whom veils, clouds and doubts did not prevent from the dwelling-place of verses.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s blessing on those whom veils, clouds and doubts did not keep from the dwelling-place of verses; keeps the note of the faithful exception.

selected.text: O people, deal fairly with this Youth, then fear God, O people of the Bayan, and deny not Him Who hath come unto you with the verses of 'Ali, then with the proof of Muhammad, and with that whereof no likeness hath appeared in all creation.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s appeal to deal fairly with the Youth Who came with the verses of ‘Ali and the proof of Muhammad.

selected.text: Fear ye God, and spread not corruption in the earth, nor follow every heedless doubter among the people of the Bayan who hath turned away from the All-Merciful, clinging to that which We sent down to My Herald whom We sent with a clear proof.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel not to follow any heedless doubter among the people of the Bayan who clings to what was sent down to His Herald.

selected.text: Fie upon the people of the Bayan, for they have exchanged the bounty of God and sold the Lord of Lords for a handful of dust, without any proof or scripture. Thus did their evil souls entice them to object to God, the Single One, the Mighty, the Praised.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the people of the Bayan selling the Lord of Lords for a handful of dust without any proof or scripture.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Fear God and reject not the truth through that which ye possess.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s brief counsel not to reject the truth through what one possesses; a concise antidote that the why of its group relies on.

selected.text: Now observe the people of the Bayan with this same insight - all recite the Bayan, yet remain veiled from its Revealer. Would that they had been content with this much, but rather they have inflicted upon the Ancient Beauty that which no soul has ever inflicted upon another.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s observation that all recite the Bayan yet remain veiled from its Revealer and inflict on the Ancient Beauty what none has inflicted.

selected.text: The satans of the Bayan have acted treacherously in the Cause of their Lord, the All-Merciful, and have conspired until the fire of sedition was kindled. By this means they desired to extinguish the light of God in His dominion and to quench the fire of God among His creatures.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s account that the satans of the Bayan conspired to kindle sedition and extinguish the light of God.

selected.text: O servant! Arise to serve and obey God, then take what hath proceeded from His exalted fingers and flowed from His most luminous and transcendent Pen. Enter then into the abode of the idolaters among the concourse of the Bayan and say: O people! Fear your Lord, the All-Merciful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s charge to a servant to take His Pen’s words into the abode of the idolaters among the concourse of the Bayan; an example of the teaching task.

selected.text: Behold, then mention what the people of the Bayan have committed, who turned away from the All-Merciful and opposed Him with such tyranny as caused the denizens of the Kingdom to lament. They cast the Most Great Ocean behind their backs, hastening toward the pond. Verily, they perceive not
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the people of the Bayan casting the Most Great Ocean behind their backs and hastening toward the pond.

selected.text: By what proof have ye established My fabrication, and by what evidence have ye proven that which ye possess is from God, the All-Forgiving, the All-Bountiful? Bring forth a verse, O people of the Bayan, if ye be of the truthful. … Be fair, by God, and reject not the truth by what ye possess
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s challenge to prove His fabrication and bring forth a verse, and His counsel not to reject the truth by what one possesses.

selected.text: We would make peace with the people of the Bayan: if they will not love Me, let them not hate Me. By God! Thou shalt find their turning away from this Light which hath shone forth from the horizons with a luminous countenance, a mighty proof and a supreme evidence.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s offer to make peace with the people of the Bayan: if they will not love Him, let them not hate Him; a distinctive note of forbearance.

selected.text: it with thee, O servant, for having sheltered him who came unto thee, and honored and glorified him. By God! Were it not for My fear of the Nimrod of the Bayan, We would have given thee glad tidings with a word that would cause the realities of those who have drunk the pure wine from the Beauty of God, the Most Manifest, the Most Luminous, to rejoice, and would rend asunder the hearts
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s blessing on a servant for sheltering and honoring one who came to him, with His remark that fear of the Nimrod of the Bayan restrains a joyful word.

selected.text: Then be thou steadfast in the Cause, for most of the people of the Bayan have turned away from Him in Whom they had believed, and have worshipped the idols of their desires, and were of those who worship idols. Sanctify thyself from these who have disbelieved after having believed and have turned away.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to be steadfast, since most of the people of the Bayan worshipped the idols of their desires.

selected.text: And when the Tablet of the Youth appeareth before thee, take it with the hand of certitude, then enter the gathering-place of the idolaters among the people of the Bayan and say: "O people! I have come unto you from the Dawning-place of the Cause of your Lord, the All-Merciful, with a manifest proof
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s commission to take the Tablet of the Youth with certitude into the gathering of the people of the Bayan and announce a manifest proof; an instance of proclamation.

selected.text: Despite such clarity, observe to what degree the people of the Bayan have arisen in hatred and enmity, clinging to the word "Mustaghath" and using the school of "Him Whom God shall make manifest" as a pretext, saying "Where is the Mustaghath?" and "Where is the school of Him Whom God shall make manifest?"
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s account of the people of the Bayan clinging to the word Mustaghath and asking for the school of Him Whom God shall make manifest; shows literalism as a pretext.

selected.text: the horizon of certitude through the power of thy Lord, the Most High, the Most Great. Then enter the dwelling-place of the ungodly among the people of the Bayan who have disbelieved in God, the Creator of earth and heaven. Say: O people! Abandon that which is vain - the Self-Subsisting hath come upon the clouds of proof. Verily, He is your Lord, the All-Merciful, upon Whom the Bayan depended
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s commission to enter the dwelling of the ungodly among the people of the Bayan and proclaim that the Self-Subsisting has come; an example of proclamation.

selected.text: Say: O people of the Bayan! Fear ye the All-Merciful, and weigh what hath been sent down from the Kingdom of proof against what ye possess. Then be fair, and be not of the wrongdoers. Beware lest the calumnies of the people or the utterances of every associating soul who hath turned away from God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, hold you back
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to weigh what has been sent down from the Kingdom of proof against what one possesses, to be fair, and not be held back by calumnies.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Strive within yourselves not to act as these idolaters acted. When the Youth of the Spirit entereth upon you with God's Book, arise instantly from your seats, then take the holy Book in your hands, then kiss it, then honor the Youth with gracious respect. By God, this shall profit your souls more than all that ye are engaged in.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to rise, take the holy Book, kiss it and honor the Youth with respect when He comes; a distinctive practical image of courtesy toward revelation.

selected.text: Some practices were early customs among the people of the Bayan which were prevalent among them and which they followed without right, as you and other loved ones know that before this Most Great Manifestation, most of the people of the Bayan practiced that which accorded with no religion or law, and which no person of intellect or insight would accept.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s note that before this Manifestation many of the people of the Bayan followed customs that accorded with no religion or law; a further ethical self-critique.

selected.text: Thou, O my God! Thou seest me oppressed amidst the people of the Furqan and those who claim to be of the Bayan. Thou knowest, O my God, that had they drunk the choice wine of inner meanings from the cup of the Bayan and recognized the Manifestation of Thy name, the All-Merciful, they would not have opposed the Beloved of all creation and the King of all worlds, nor would they have denied Him Whose praise and remembrance the Tongue of Grandeur hath ever spoken
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that had the people drunk the wine of inner meanings from the Bayan they would not have opposed the Beloved of all creation.

selected.text: shouldst thou find any among the people of the Bayan who have turned away from this resplendent Countenance, say: "O thou that art far removed! If thou didst believe in the Bayan, by what proof hast thou rejected the Beloved of the worlds? By God! Not a word was revealed except in My remembrance and praise, nor was he raised up save to proclaim My Cause
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s instruction to ask any who turned away by what proof they rejected the Beloved, since not a word of the Bayan was revealed except in His remembrance.

selected.text: In these wondrous Tablets, newly revealed and sent forth from the Most Holy and Most Glorious Court, observe how during this period all the people of the Bayan, without exception--even unto the most exalted among them--have been heedless of the essence of the Cause. Would that after all this heedlessness shown during this time, they might now become mindful and make amends for the past
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s observation that all the people of the Bayan were heedless of the essence of the Cause, and His hope that they might now make amends.

selected.text: the Bayan - they have disbelieved in God just as did the people before them. They are indeed among the most lost. O Karim! God willing, thou shalt be blessed through His grace and stand firm in His Cause. In most times thy call hath been heard and the Most Exalted Pen hath moved at thy name. Know thou the measure of this mighty station, and as thou gazest upon the name of the Lord of Power, preserve it. Reflect upon the baseness of the people of the Bayan - they have turned away from One from Whose pen flowed the equivalent of all the books on earth and all tidings past and future, and they busy themselves with their own vain imaginings. Fie
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s contrast between the baseness of those who turned from One Whose pen equalled all books and His blessing on a steadfast believer.

selected.text: Fie upon them! It is most certain, evident and proven that every previous Manifestation hath given glad tidings of the subsequent Revelation according to the stations and capacities of the people - some through allusion and some through subtle intimations. But the previous Manifestation, beyond what can be conceived and comprehended, strove in counseling and educating the people of the Bayan. Yet that which came to pass came to pass.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that every Manifestation gave glad tidings of the next, and that the Báb strove beyond conception to educate the people of the Bayan; frames progressive revelation.

selected.text: They have abandoned the Mother Book and clung to their own desires through the book of perdition. Today the Mother Book calleth out before the faces of all people: O ye that slumber, arise! O ye that are heedless, become aware! Today the world is perfumed by the breezes of the dawn of revelation and illumined by the light of His countenance. Abandon the dawning-places of vain imaginings and break the idols of idle fancies with the arm of certitude.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s summons from the Mother Book to the slumbering to arise and break the idols of idle fancies with the arm of certitude; a memorable call to awaken.

selected.text: Consider those who claim to belong to the Bayan. They have turned away from the All-Merciful and speak that which causeth the heavens and earth to laugh at them. Among them is he who hath said that He hath claimed Divinity, and that we must not believe in this exalted station. Say: He Who gave you glad tidings of His Own Self hath said that He speaketh in all things, "there is no God but Me, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved." We see them to be more lost in understanding than the people of the Furqan, nay than those of all religions.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s reply to the objection that He claimed Divinity, citing the Báb that He speaks in all things “there is no God but Me”.

selected.text: the people of the Bayan, like unto the people of the Furqan, have clung to vain imaginings and idle fancies, and are diligently engaged in leading the servants astray. Not for a moment have they pondered what the fruits of the deeds, words and beliefs of the Shi'ih party have been. By God! They are in manifest delusion
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s observation that the people of the Bayan, like the people of the Furqan, have not pondered the fruits of the deeds and beliefs of the Shi’ih party.

selected.text: Until now, the people of the Bayan have not perceived the fragrance of the Day of God, nor have they become aware of the hidden mysteries in the blessed word "He doeth whatsoever He willeth." They have not attained even a drop of this ocean. Blindly and ignorantly they run about and speak. At times they mention the alteration of the Bayan, and at other times they speak of other matters. They have contrived calumnies that perchance they might thereby conceal the lights of the Sun of the supreme horizon. In truth, they are seen to be the most lost among the parties of the world.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the people of the Bayan have missed the hidden mysteries of “He doeth whatsoever He willeth” and contrived calumnies; carries the guide’s point about divine freedom.

selected.text: O people of the Bayan! Do ye read the verses while denying their Revealer? By God the Truth! None hath done as ye have done, nor have any peoples committed what ye have committed. Woe unto you, O company of evil ones! Ye have indeed failed in your own selves, to such extent that ye have forgotten God's covenant, broken His testament, and turned away from Him by Whose command ye and the heavens and earth were created. There is no God but Him. His is the creation and the command. He sendeth down what He willeth to whom He willeth, and all things are decreed in His presence.
selected.reason: Addresses reading revealed verses while denying their Revealer.
